hōrologium, hōrologiī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a clock

Classically a sundial or a water clock (Lewis & Short); the word has served for every kind of clock since. A wall clock is hōrologium parietārium, an alarm clock hōrologium excitātōrium.

Other words

  • hōrae, hōrārum f. pl. — the clock (on a tower)

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. clock, citing Vives, Exercitatio 297: īnspice hōrās · Declension on Wiktionary

    Vives’s schoolboys look at “the hours” on a church clock; not a classical use.

Examples

  • Īnspice hōrologium: quota hōra est?

    Look at the clock: what time is it?composed

  • Hōrologium rēctē mētītur.

    The clock keeps good time.Traupman 122

  • hōrologium temperāre

    to set the clockTraupman 122

  • hōrologium intendere

    to wind the clockTraupman 122

See also wall clock, alarm clock, wristwatch, check the time, hourglass.
